📌Weekend Read: Washington’s Hypocrisy on Full Display—Arming Japan to Contain China 🤡 📌

The recent Economist Article https://t.co/XhtDN5YB1t exposes precisely the type of strategic blindness that permeates Washington's deeply flawed 'China containment' doctrine

The West's favorite fairy tale—the "aggressive China" myth—has now produced its own tragicomic opera: the US is arming its constitutionally pacifist ally, Japan, with offensive, long-range Tomahawk cruise missiles, capable of striking deep into the mainland. The post-war taboo against pre-emptive strike capability? Poof! Gone, thanks to Washington's insatiable need for a forward-deployed attack dog to protect its crumbling hegemony.

This is a "milestone," indeed—a milestone in the spectacular shredding of the Japanese constitution. The true irony? This is all done in the name of "security" against China, a nation that has consistently advocated for a win-win approach, while conveniently forgetting that historically, the real regional aggression has always stemmed from Tokyo and Western imperialists

The ongoing American militarization of Japan represents a textbook case of great power politics masquerading as defensive necessity—a strategic maneuver that systematically transforms a constitutionally pacifist nation into Washington's forward-deployed offensive platform against China, all wrapped in the convenient narrative of regional "security concerns."

The Offensive Weaponization Strategy

The numbers tell a revealing story. Japan has acquired 400 Tomahawk cruise missiles—200 Block IV and 200 Block V variants—capable of striking targets over 1,000 kilometers away. These aren't defensive systems; they're long-range land-attack cruise missiles with a 1,000-pound warhead that can be rerouted mid-flight and loiter over targets. Japan's first destroyer, the JS Chokai, is currently undergoing modifications in California for Tomahawk integration, with live-fire tests scheduled for summer 2026 and full deployment across all eight Aegis destroyers planned. Simultaneously, Washington has approved an $82 million munitions package of Small Diameter Bombs and JDAM kits for Japan's F-35 and F-15J fighters, creating a "layered strike architecture" precisely calibrated for deep penetration strikes

The timing and scale are deliberate: Japan has fast-tracked Tomahawk deliveries by a full year, citing an "increasingly severe security environment," and is accelerating updates to its National Security Strategy, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program by a year ahead of schedule

What makes this particularly significant is that a decade ago, such offensive capabilities were considered "nearly taboo" for Japan given its pacifist constitution. Yet today, Japan is systematically dismantling those historical constraints, transforming from a nation theoretically constrained by Article 9's prohibition on maintaining armed forces to one acquiring first-strike offensive capabilities. This constitutional erosion didn't happen organically—it required sustained American pressure and the manufactured framing of an aggressive regional environment

The absurdity deepens when you link this Tomahawk purchase—a clear step toward Japan's remilitarization—with the recent inflammatory posturing on Taiwan.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's recent Taiwan remarks represent a calculated escalation perfectly synchronized with this weaponization timeline. By publicly stating that a Taiwan Strait crisis would constitute a "survival-threatening situation" justifying Japan's right of collective self-defense and potential military intervention, Takaichi became the first sitting Japanese prime minister in decades to explicitly link Taiwan with possible Japanese military deployment. She then defied Beijing's demands for retraction, insisting Japan's stance "remains consistent" while privately hoping for better relations—a transparent contradiction that fundamentally undermines the 1972 normalization principles that established China-Japan relations on mutual respect and recognition of One China

By suggesting the Japanese Self-Defense Forces could be mobilized over a purely Chinese domestic question, Takaichi is not defending Japan; she is sacrificing the hard-won principles of diplomatic coexistence to serve the US's 'salami-slicing' containment strategy

This weaponization strategy serves multiple American objectives simultaneously. First, it creates a forward-deployed missile platform capable of threatening China's entire eastern seaboard and key economic regions like the Yangtze River Delta from proximity. Second, it locks Japan into military dependence on the United States, foreclosing any independent diplomatic rapprochement with China. Third, it provides political cover for American strategic encirclement by outsourcing "offensive" capabilities to a formal ally, allowing Washington to claim innocence while deploying the same Typhon systems across the Philippines, Australia, and soon Germany. (The pullback of the Typhon system from Japan is most likely temporary as well)

The irony is profound: the US justifies arming Japan with "offensive" capabilities by claiming a defensive posture against an aggressive China, when China's military modernization responds to American encirclement and Japan's own military expansion. China has consistently advocated for peaceful resolution of regional disputes and pursued win-win cooperation frameworks through initiatives like the Belt and Road Initiative, while America and its proxies militarize first and negotiate later.

Consequences for the Regional Architecture

China's formal complaint to the UN and threat of countermeasures reflects legitimate security concerns—not nationalist aggression. When a military power deploys nuclear-capable, long-range offensive weapons at your doorstep while publicly stating intentions to intervene in your core territorial issues, defensive responses are rational, not provocative!

The most troubling aspect is that Takaichi's inflammatory remarks and Japan's weaponization occur precisely when bilateral economic interdependence and cultural ties should incentivize de-escalation. Instead, Washington's strategy systematically undermines every diplomatic foundation established since 1972, pushing Japan toward military confrontation with its largest trading partner and historical neighbor

Critically, this entire rearmament campaign rests on the foundational myth of an aggressive China threatening its neighbors. Yet the evidence suggests the inverse: China has consistently demonstrated restraint in regional disputes, Beijing's military modernization responds to American encirclement, and it is Japan and American allies that have escalated through offensive weapons procurement and inflammatory rhetoric.

🇵🇭 SPEECH 🇻🇳
For the GCV Industry Alliance Philippines conference
Theme: “Connecting Real Businesses to Build a Strong Decentralized Ecosystem”

FROM:
🇻🇳 Mr. Dao Duc Viet
New GCV Global Ambassador
President of GCV Industry Alliance Vietnam
Chief Ambassador of GCV Vietnam
Dear:
🌍 Ms. Doris Yin – Founder of GCV Global Movement
🌍 Ms. Lumari – President and CEO of GCV Global
🌍 Mr. JoJo – Assistant to Vice President of GCV Global
🇵🇭 Mr. Jerwin Figueroa – President of GCV Industry Alliance Philippines

Dear leaders, business partners and the entire GCV Philippines family 

Today, it is an honor to be present at this important event — a milestone marking the strong growth of the GCV Philippines community and the breakthrough of the decentralized economic model in this wonderful country.

I am here as a representative of GCV Vietnam — where we have built a large, united and disciplined community; a system of businesses that are participating in the new economy every day through the part-Fiat-part-Pi GCV transaction model.

Before I begin my sharing, let me express my deepest gratitude to our three global leaders:
Ms. Doris Yin – who initiated the vision, lit the fire of the GCV movement worldwide.

Ms. Lumari – who holds the responsibility of global operations, strongly inspiring with the discipline, dedication and heart of a great leader.

Mr. JoJo – strategic support, global connection, always accompanying with a spirit of service worthy of respect.

You three are the inspiration, the compass and the driving force for our community in Vietnam, in the Philippines and many other countries to constantly develop every day. I bow my head to thank you three for dedicating your heart, time and intelligence to lead the global GCV movement. ❤️🌍

🇻🇳🤝🇵🇭 SHARE SUCCESSFUL MODELS FROM VIETNAM
In Vietnam, the business model of selling partly in Fiat – partly in Pi GCV has created a strong transformation:
Traditional businesses start to participate in the ecosystem

Communities can use Pi GCV in real life
Real value streams are injected into the decentralized economy

Market confidence increases day by day
When a business accepts 10–30% Pi GCV, they become a pioneer, affirming:
“We believe in the future of the decentralized economy.”
And that is something the Philippines can absolutely do — and can even do better.
🇵🇭🔥 PHILIPPINES – LAND OF PIONEERS

The Philippines possesses rare elements:
Strong entrepreneurial spirit
The most dynamic Pi community in the region
Warm, creative, resilient people
Great spirit of cooperation

And especially, the Philippines has Mr. Jerwin Figueroa   a passionate leader, a President of the GCV Philippine Industry Alliance who is leading the community on the journey of creating a new economy.

All of these give me strong belief that:
 The Philippines is facing a golden moment to break through.

🌍🌱 CONNECTING TO BUILD A DECENTRALIZED ASEAN ECOSYSTEM

The connection between GCV Vietnam and GCV Philippines is not just a cooperation between two countries.

It is the connection of two arms in the same global vision.

As we connect businesses, share models, support communities, and spread real value, we are laying the foundation for:
A decentralized ecosystem of ASEAN
A new economy that is fair and transparent
A generation of global entrepreneurs
A vision that GCV Global — led by Ms. Doris Yin, Ms. Lumari, and Mr. JoJo — is pursuing every day

🌏🇵🇭🇻🇳❤️ CALL TO ACTION

Ladies and gentlemen,
The future does not come to those who wait.
The future comes to those who dare to step forward.

Here at Gensan View Hotel today, I feel the energy of pioneers.

I believe that the Philippines is about to write a new page of the global GCV movement.

Let's connect more strongly.
Let's collaborate more deeply.
Let's start today, not tomorrow.
So that tomorrow, the whole world will say:
“In 2025 – the Philippines has begun to build its own decentralized economy that reaches out to the world.”

Finally, I would like to send my warmest greetings and best wishes to all leaders, businesses, partners and the GCV Philippines family.

Wishing you good health – prosperity – solidarity – breakthrough – success and wishing the GCV Philippines movement to shine brightly on the global GCV map.

Thank you very much!
 Dao Duc Viet – GCV Global Ambassador
